title: console-observability-triage-scratchpad-samir-2026-03-25
content:
Console / Observability triage scratchpad - Samir Rao
Dates: created 2026-03-24, updated 2026-03-25

Quick context:
- Customer A reported that the per-route latency heatmap in the Console shows spikes during 10:00-11:00 PST yesterday but their app-level traces don’t show corresponding tail latency. They see timeouts at 11:03. Ticket JIRA:OBS-4821 (priority P1 for customer-impact).
- Internal dashboards: route-latency, gpu-queue-depth, batch-size-distribution. Noticed dropped metrics for gpu-queue-depth for region-us-west-2 between 10:45-11:15.
- Related: OBS-4823 is a UI bug where the heatmap color-scale compresses values > 200ms to same color; makes triage harder.

Today goals (quick):
- Reproduce customer timeline locally / sandbox (10:00-11:30 window) -> check request routing + fallbacks.
- Confirm if metrics gap for gpu-queue-depth is ingestion or display glitch.
- Patch heatmap scale UI bug (OBS-4823) or at least add tooltip with exact values so CS can see numbers.
- Follow-up with CS owner (Priya) with temporary workaround and ETA.

Notes / steps taken:
- 09:30 — pulled logs for customer A (tenant-id 0xA33F) via s3://redwood-logs/prod/us-west-2/2026-03-24/ -> found 11:02:59 request with status 504, route pinned to model-rw-7B-quantized-2.
- Checked trace sampling: only 5% capture; raised to 50% for that tenant for 24h (temp) to get more data. Patch sent as deployment request to platform (PR #1258).
- Querying metrics: grafana query for gpu_queue_depth shows null series for host group rwd-usw2-gpupool-3 between 10:46-11:12. Possible exporter restart?
- Checked infra alerts: no node restarts flagged in SRE page for that window. But k8s events show kubelet OOMKill on rwd-usw2-node-17 at 10:47. correlate? maybe exporter process crashed -> metrics gap.
- Replayed a small load in sandbox (same model + sequence length) -> observed increased queue depth and slowdowns, but not the abrupt gap. Means gap likely due to exporter/agent missing rather than actual absence of queue.

Hypothesis:
1) The customer timeout at 11:03 is due to transient overload + missing fallback to CPU model variant (policy mis-evaluated). Need to confirm routing policy decision logs.
2) The metrics gap is exporter/agent downtime on rwd-usw2-node-17 that masked the gradual increase; UI heatmap exaggerated because it compresses higher values.

Immediate next actions (today):
- [ ] Attach routing decision logs for affected requests (Samir) -> query logs: request_decisions.service logs (PR: log export already enabled for that range).
- [ ] Ask SRE to check node rwd-usw2-node-17 for exporter process health and restart reason (Eden). Tag SRE on OBS-4821.
- [ ] Quick UI patch: change heatmap scale to logarithmic / add hover numbers (small PR to dashboard repo) (Samir -> estimate 2-3h). If not possible, add tooltip that shows exact ms values so CS can triage.
- [ ] Draft reply to customer w/ temporary workaround: suggest pinning to dedicated capacity or enabling model-variant fallback and raise trace sampling (Priya to send).

Follow-ups / longer term:
- Increase exporter process monitoring and add alert when metrics series goes stale for >1m (SRE / infra work).
- Consider exposing per-route decision reasons in Console (helpful for customer support; low friction) -> product discussion item.
- Heatmap color-scale: move to percentile buckets instead of absolute ms to avoid compression issues across customers. Add to product backlog if OBS-4823 fix is heavier.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Did autoscaler do anything odd for that pool at 10:40-11:10? check dedicated autoscale logs (where are they stored — link?). TODO: find autoscaler log path.
- Need to verify whether fallback policy was disabled for that tenant (policy id?). Ask product (Eden) / PM.
- Should we temporarily increase default trace-sampling for any tenant hitting >X error rate? config change discussion.

Short-term communications draft (for CS / Priya):
- "We investigated and saw a node-level exporter gap in metrics which hid a growing GPU queue depth. We also saw a routing decision that did not fall back to a compatible model variant; we’re investigating why the policy didn’t trigger. Temporary mitigation: enable model-variant fallback for your route, and we can pin you to dedicated capacity for the affected window. We’ll follow up with more details once SRE confirms node health logs."

Random notes / reminders to self:
- Save logs for 2026-03-24/10:30-11:30 to obs-archive bucket before rotation.
- If sandbox replay reproduces high latency, capture pprof on model runtime.
- Add link to dashboard panel that shows exporter uptime (not available currently) -> quick query to add to default triage dashboard.

Edits / history:
- 2026-03-24 09:40 - started note; added initial queries.
- 2026-03-24 12:10 - found kubelet OOMKill on node-17, flagged to SRE.
- 2026-03-25 08:20 - increased trace sampling for tenant; created PR #1258 to enable temporary sampling change.

End scratchpad.
